original_question: Let K be a compact space such that the Baire sigma-algebras Ba(C(K), T_p) and Ba(C(K), w) coincide, where T_p is the topology of pointwise convergence on K. Must every probability measure in P(K) belong to the weak*-sequential closure Seq(co(Δ_K)) of the convex hull of the point-evaluation measures Δ_K = {δ_t : t ∈ K}?
target_in_paper: Problem 2.2 in Section 2.1 of arXiv:1607.07787, which is the survey restatement of the equivalent reformulation of Conjecture 1.1 from Avilés–Plebanek–Rodríguez, On Baire measurability in spaces of continuous functions, using Proposition 1.2.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right compact-space setting, the right two Baire σ-algebras on C(K) (pointwise vs. weak), the right measure space P(K), and the right conclusion involving the weak*-sequential closure of the convex hull of the Dirac measures. In substance, it matches Problem 2.2 of the survey and the Proposition 1.2 reformulation of the original conjecture.
missing_details: The paper works with compact Hausdorff spaces K.
C(K) means the real Banach space of continuous real-valued functions on K.
The standard paper notation is C_p(K) and C_w(K), not just C(K) with T_p and w.
P(K) denotes the regular Borel probability measures on K, identified with a subset of C(K)^* = M(K).
The closure is taken for the weak* topology on C(K)^* (equivalently on P(K)).
Seq(co(Δ_K)) means the smallest weak*-sequentially closed subset containing co(Δ_K), not merely the set of first-step sequential limits of sequences from co(Δ_K).
co(Δ_K) is exactly the set of finitely supported probability measures on K, since Δ_K = {δ_t : t ∈ K}.

The original paper's primary formulation is slightly more local: it asks about a single Ba(C_p(K))-measurable probability measure μ, and Proposition 1.2 converts that to your global σ-algebra-equality formulation.
To make the question fully stand-alone, one should state that μ is viewed as the linear functional f ↦ ∫_K f dμ on C(K).
refined_question: Let K be a compact Hausdorff space, let C_p(K) and C_w(K) denote the Banach space C(K) of continuous real-valued functions on K endowed respectively with the pointwise and weak topologies, and identify P(K) with the set of regular Borel probability measures on K inside C(K)^* equipped with the weak* topology. If a measure μ ∈ P(K), viewed as the linear functional f ↦ ∫_K f dμ on C(K), is measurable with respect to Ba(C_p(K)), must μ belong to Seq(co(Δ_K)), where Δ_K = {δ_t : t ∈ K} and Seq(co(Δ_K)) is the smallest weak*-sequentially closed subset of P(K) containing co(Δ_K)?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by Proposition 1.2, if Ba(C_p(K)) = Ba(C_w(K)), must every probability measure on K belong to Seq(co(Δ_K)); that is, must P(K) = Seq(co(Δ_K))?
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper's measurability-versus-sequential-closure problem. In the survey arXiv:1607.07787, this appears verbatim as Problem 2.2. In the original paper, however, the principal statement is Conjecture 1.1, formulated for an individual probability measure μ that is Ba(C_p(K))-measurable. Proposition 1.2 gives the bridge from that formulation to your draft by identifying the hypothesis Ba(C_p(K)) = Ba(C_w(K)) with the statement that every μ ∈ P(K) is Ba(C_p(K))-measurable. Theorem 1.3 is part of the immediate introductory context showing why the paper uses the full operator Seq(co(Δ_K)) rather than only first-step sequential limits, so the refined question keeps exactly that stronger sequential-closure notion.
